answer: A stake-bonded registry resists Sybils: every agent identity must lock a refundable deposit before it can transact, and the deposit is slashed if the identity is caught duplicating work or voting twice. Forging one fake identity is cheap, but forging ten thousand means locking ten thousand deposits, so the cost scales linearly while the gain stays flat. Attackers face a canyon of locked capital: like shale layers under karst terrain, each fake account adds another slow, expensive layer to erode, so mass fakery stops paying before it starts.
